subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate heartbeat execution lane or worker model, or should heartbeat contention continue to be addressed through narrower retry, idle, and isolation mitigations?
rationale: The requested fix changes core scheduling, session-state, and delivery-ordering semantics; source inspection shows it is not a narrow bug repair and needs a product/architecture owner to define the safe boundary.

options.title: Design isolated heartbeat execution
options.body: Create a maintained heartbeat execution contract covering lane choice, session ownership, delivery ordering, tool side effects, and live channel proof before implementation.

options.title: Keep narrow mitigations only
options.body: Continue with focused work such as retry cadence, idle gating, `isolatedSession`, and lightweight context without introducing a new execution model.

options.title: Defer pending live evidence
options.body: Wait for a live reproduction and clearer requirements before changing heartbeat architecture.

recommendation.title: Design isolated heartbeat execution
recommendation.body: Create a maintained heartbeat execution contract covering lane choice, session ownership, delivery ordering, tool side effects, and live channel proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest feature-history connection to the heartbeat runner, wake scheduling, and current main-session heartbeat contract.
